links.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of ChatGPT responses to patient strabismus questions
links.effect: Average Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 15, higher than high school reading level; low readability.
links.quote: On average, responses scored a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level score of 15, equating to a higher than high school grade reading level.

links.outcome: Reading level of chatbot answers relative to patient reading level
links.effect: Mean FK grade level 15, exceeding high school level, demonstrating low readability.
links.quote: The average reading level exceeded a high school level and demonstrated low readability.

links.outcome: Consistency of response accuracy across repeated runs, time points, and locations
links.effect: Acceptable responses 77% California vs 51% Florida (P<.001); inaccurate/harmful 6.9% vs 1.5%; acceptable 60% day 0, 64% 1 week, 67% 1 month.
links.quote: Although most of ChatGPT's responses to strabismus questions were clinically acceptable, there were variations in responses across time and geographic regions.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the baseline accuracy, safety, and readability of ChatGPT (GPT-3.5 and GPT-4) responding to patient questions about strabismus, without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
